correctness.rationale: For a cactus graph, the signed simple-cycle sums have edge-disjoint supports and form an integral basis of \(H_1\). The explicit edgewise averaging map is a chain extension of norm \(1/g(X)\). Conversely, cointegrality forces every nonzero integral shortest-cycle class to have integral coordinate \(\ell^1\)-norm at least \(1\); applying any chain extension to that cycle yields \(1\le g(X)\|s\|^B\). These bounds match and all quantifiers in the gnarledness definition are respected. The geometric comparison uses the relative basis of non-tree edges. No computation is substituted for an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Algebraic gnarledness is newly introduced as a universal quantitative chain-complex invariant. The cactus family is a standard, structurally motivated class in which first homology may have arbitrary rank while cycle supports remain disjoint. The exact value \(1/g(X)\) identifies a familiar graph invariant as the complete quantitative answer and proves that basis mixing cannot improve it. Combining with the known geometric value \(1\) gives an exact unbounded separation, so the result is more than a routine recomputation of a single example.
